text: The goal is to provide unemployed clients who are able to work easier access to employment assistance so that they can get back to work sooner.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: They can also get more holistic support and assistance, with employment goals tied closely to social assistance.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: This is one of the many ways that MSF innovates to make service delivery more client-centric.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We will continue to explore other possible ways to make it easier for those in need to get the help they need and to do so in a manner that does not diminish personal responsibility, self-reliance, as well as family and community support.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We are making progress in better supporting persons with disabilities.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: The recommendations range from improving the quality of lives of persons with disabilities and supporting their caregivers, to building up the community's capabilities in supporting them and charting the way forward in building an inclusive society.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: The recommendations highlight the importance of building an ecosystem of support for persons with disabilities in enabling them as integral and contributing members of our society.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Family members form the core in the ecosystem of support.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: The larger community, comprising the health, education and social services and the society at large, provides the other layers of support in the ecosystem.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: My Ministry will continue to work on strengthening this ecosystem in enabling more holistic support and a smoother transition for persons with disabilities at different stages of their lives.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We will also continue to ensure Singapore remains a great place to raise children and form stable families.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: For families facing challenges, we will continue to support them at critical junctures of their lives, to strengthen both immediate and extended family bonds.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: It is every parent's hope that their child can start off on a strong footing.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: KidSTART seeks to proactively identify children aged six and below, provide them with early access to health, learning and developmental support, as well as monitor their progress during their early years.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Under KidSTART today, some Anchor Operator centres are provided additional manpower to engage Child Enabling Executives to work closely with parents of low-income and vulnerable children enrolled at these centres, and, if need be, work with parents to improve their children's attendance.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Parents and partners have responded positively to the support provided under KidSTART so far.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We have also been receiving encouraging feedback on improved parent-child interaction and preschool attendance.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: While good efforts have been made, we know very well that our work is not finished.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: There are many opportunities ahead for us to improve the quality of our lives, and extend our help to vulnerable ones.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: To achieve our vision of a caring society, the Government's efforts alone are not enough.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: (In English): Mdm Chairman, I would like to thank all Members for sharing their thoughts on fostering a more caring Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: As we progressed economically in the past 50 years, we created opportunities for Singaporeans to pursue their dreams and to provide for their families.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Individual effort, strong families and active involvement by the community remain important principles.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Our growth also allowed us to enhance support for families and to give our children a good start, regardless of background.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We increased assistance to those who need help and improved the quality of life for the elderly and persons with disabilities.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: While our elderly enjoy longer life expectancy, they also require sufficient resources to see them through their twilight years.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: More of them are developing disabilities as they age.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Family structures are evolving as we have more choosing to remain single or childless, or living alone.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We are also seeing more remarriages and intercultural marriages.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Social services, therefore, have been expanding to meet these needs.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: But like many sectors, getting more manpower to keep pace with demand remains a continuing challenge.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: During the Budget debate, Members spoke about new economic realities, such as evolving business models, disruptions and labour market uncertainties.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: It will probably mean that more persons will require support and, probably, for longer periods, during job transitions.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Therefore, it is imperative for us to take a whole-of-Government approach to enable all Singaporeans, including the vulnerable, to adapt to these changes.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Keeping our economy healthy with good jobs growth remains key because it helps our people stay employed.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We will also help workers to upgrade their skills on an ongoing basis, so that they remain relevant as the economy evolves.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We will also help with job matching where we can.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: While seemingly economic in nature, I would suggest that many of the measures taken by CFE and with SkillsFuture have a lot of bearing on our social well-being as well.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: But, lastly, invariably, where individuals fall on hard times, this is where the social safety net − by which I mean families, the community and the Government − will all have to come together to strengthen support.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We believe that, as we help, we must foster hope for the future and a very real improvement in lives.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: If Members noticed, and many of us often ask, what is MSF doing, what is the Government doing?

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: But I think it is important for us to realise that we all have a role to play.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: So, I would like to reiterate these principles and values that I believe should guide us.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Every Singaporean must be able to stand on their own two feet and live a life of dignity.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Enabling those who can work to work helps to maintain self-respect and empowers one to improve his or her circumstances.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We must not only help individuals with short-term needs, but help them to help themselves in the long term.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Families, we all know, form the foundation of any society and, definitely, in our society, and they should be the first line of support.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Family bonds help us get through tough times.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Imagine a society where, when there are troubles, the first thing people ask is not so much what are the families doing, what is the individual doing, but what is the community doing about it.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: I think it would represent something that we should be worried about.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: But I think these are values that many of us continue to hold true today.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: The wider community plays a part, which is all of us here, as leaders in our own respective spaces.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: I think different players − some of you have suggested about how volunteers can play a part − and, certainly, different players like VWOs, grassroots, philanthropists and volunteers from all walks of life – can and should come together to provide care and support in big and small ways and they, definitely, augment the support provided by the Government.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: So, we need to prepare for the future.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: At the same time, we still have to pay attention to sustainability, to ensure that resources are going to where they are most needed.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: My Parliamentary Secretary and I will be elaborating on the Ministry's work in three key areas.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: An inclusive society is one where each Singaporean is enabled to lead a fulfilling life, regardless of their starting point.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Developing this sense of inclusiveness is and has to be a whole-of-society effort.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: The family plays a critical role in preserving a closely-knit society and in serving as a pillar of support for individuals.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We want to ensure that Singapore remains a great place to raise children and give them a good start in life.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We want to establish stable family units, while supporting families that do face difficulties.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: A strong family goes a long way in helping individuals overcome challenges.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: I am talking not just about immediate family, but also the extended family.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: As individual family units come under strain, such as through difficult life events like illness, extended family members can play an important role in providing support, especially when family units are becoming smaller.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: However, there will be families whose ties have been weakened and help from within is not immediately available.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: And that is where the Government and community partners, neighbours, can help them to resolve their issues and rebuild their ties.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: My Parliamentary Secretary will speak on how we will strengthen and support families through better childcare and infant care services, as well as early intervention measures for young families.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: He will also outline how we will help families to mend fractured ties, and how we should deal with domestic violence.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Thirdly, we will enrich our social assets by Strengthening the People Sector.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Our community partners are doing very, very good work and I urge them to continue.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Given the nature and complexity of needs, all of us need to play our part to provide holistic help to those in need.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: This way, we can achieve greater impact and we can scale what we do.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: When you scale, you can begin to go upstream and look at preventing problems and not just dealing with problems when they happen.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: So, developing our social service organisations, as well as enabling and empowering caring communities, continues to be an important priority for MSF.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: At the end of the day, all our efforts − family, community and Government − contribute towards our vision of a caring and inclusive society.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: For this first section, I will elaborate on our work in building an inclusive society.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Individuals who are disadvantaged and have complex needs will feel the challenges of livelihood most acutely.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: If displaced from their jobs, they might not have sufficient savings or other sources of income to tide them through these rough patches.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Those without family support will require greater support from the community and the Government.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: It is not only about extending more help.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We need to be innovative to help them more holistically and try to break the cycle of disadvantage.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Just providing and disbursing help is the easy part in some sense, but helping them to break out of the circumstances so that they can fundamentally change their circumstances, that is where the important work lies.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Another group that we will strengthen support for are persons with disabilities.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: They face different challenges and, invariably, have less options than the rest of us.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: In the past few years, we have made good progress in areas, such as early intervention, education, employment and in raising awareness and recognition of persons with disabilities.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: I will elaborate more on our plans, starting with how we intend to support those who need financial help.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: In recent years, we have progressively strengthened our social safety nets.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: The SSOs are the cornerstone of our social assistance framework.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: For seniors who may require social assistance but are unable to travel to the office, our officers can conduct the assessment at their homes.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: For immobile seniors who are already on our schemes, our officers can also directly credit the payment to agencies for their household bills if there is such a request or when officers assess that doing so will be helpful to the seniors.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Ms Sylvia Lim asked about some of these possible arrangements.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Being forward deployed, SSOs develop a good sense of the local community's needs and enjoy better collaboration.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: The SSOs are not the only players in the community.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: There are various stakeholders, VWOs, FSCs, so the partnership with them also enables the SSOs to get a better feel of the situation on the ground.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: What are some of the products as a result of these partnerships?

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: For instance, one of the SSOs has partnered North East CDC to pay for pest control services to assist rental flat residents deal with their bed bugs.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: In Bukit Merah, for example, our SSO initiated a Spooner Road POW WOW platform where all partners could coordinate their action plan for vulnerable families in the area.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: This enabled clients to be better served in a holistic manner and avoided duplication of effort among the agencies.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: The various partner agencies continue to meet through this platform to share best practices and resolve complex cases.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: This is something that we want to encourage, we want to see it happening on a wider basis.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Some of us, as advisors, are playing an active role trying to pull together the different stakeholders.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: It is important for the stakeholders to get together because when they talk, they build relationships, they exchange information, that is when there is real coordination and the real coordinated work happens on the ground.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Mr Faisal Manap also asked about the training received by SSO officers.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Officers also undergo training in areas pertinent to their work, such as engagement and interviewing skills, the assessment of needs and financial literacy.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: It is also important to realise, as I mentioned earlier, that the SSO does not exist on its own.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: It works very closely with the local Family Service Centre where the social workers will then follow up with the individual clients.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: There are also other players, such as the SAC and other stakeholders where the partnership is established.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: So, the social work community that exists on the ground comprises SSOs and the key partners who work together to try and address some of the needs that our residents face.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Mr Faisal Manap and Ms Sylvia Lim asked about the ComCare Scheme.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We have extended the coverage to more families.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: So, basically, we have extended the coverage in terms of those who may need ComCare assistance.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We have also increased the quantum of Long-Term Assistance.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: The rates were also increased for larger households.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Households may also receive additional support to meet other needs, such as medical consumables, adult diapers and one-off items like commodes and wheelchairs for their frail elderly.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: So, these are some of the ad hoc needs that may sometimes arise and assistance can be provided.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: At the individual-level, SSO officers are empowered to exercise flexibility when providing social assistance to low-income families under the ComCare scheme.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: It is important for officers not to just follow a rule rigidly.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: But the space is accorded to them to make some of these discretionary calls.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Our officers will then calibrate both the amount and the duration of Short-to-Medium-Term Assistance according to the different needs of families.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: For one-off and ad-hoc expenses, as mentioned by Mr Faisal Manap, they also exercise flexibility and also tap on community resources to assist.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: I think many of us are familiar, at the CDC level, initiatives are initiated by us, working with the various stakeholders − the local merchants, the local VWOs.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Collectively, we also help to provide some of these means to assist individuals on a need basis.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We do want to help families get back on their feet, but some will progress faster than others.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Ms Sylvia Lim asked, "How do you measure?" The honest truth is that it is actually quite difficult.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Is it about the numbers we are talking about?

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: By extending the coverage, we do have more numbers of those we are assisting.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Is it about how long they remain on help?

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: But the reality is that it really depends.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Some are temporary because they have lost their jobs, so they need something to tide them over.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Others have more chronic family problems, but they are not work-capable; some have health issues and that is a bit more long-drawn.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: But the key thing is: when they need help, are we able to provide help?

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: And even though it may be short or medium-term, it does not mean that after a few months, we will cut it off.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We do have the capacity and we do actually extend it when they continue to have those issues.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Of course, those on long-term assistance are very different.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We will review them from time to time.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: For those on Short-to-Medium-Term Assistance, we will adjust accordingly and will not cut off the assistance prematurely.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: And if you do meet individuals who seem to have some of these challenges, do flag it to us and let us know because we will be quite happy to adjust as we do make those accommodations.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: As we all know, on the ground, the stories that we receive are not always necessarily complete.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: But, when in doubt, surface it and we will be more than happy to assess it.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: So, we do look at it from a needs-based approach and we consider all sources of income.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Ms Sylvia Lim also asked about Silver Support.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: For those on Short-to-Medium-Term Assistance, there will be some that are not receiving Silver Support.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We are also quite mindful as to how to calibrate the amount.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: So, Silver Support is factored in for the Short-to-Medium-Term assistance recipients.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Ms Denise Phua asked about families facing problems with debt and arrears.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: In fact, I was just having a discussion on this recently with an expert from overseas.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: That is a very simple step, but it goes a very long way and, for many, it makes a lot of difference.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: For example, it allows these families to go on instalment plans.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Concurrently, our officers will assess the family's situation and they will look at ComCare to support their basic living expenses, if necessary.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Can you imagine a scenario where, if you are in debt and, therefore, public monies are then re-directed to service your debt?

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Basically, exploring different ideas to see how best to equip our social workers with the ability to integrate financial advice into their intervention plans for vulnerable families.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: So, we welcome partners who are keen to explore such solutions.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: I am aware that Methodist Welfare Services provides some of these.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: I think it is too early to conclude.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: And for those who are operating in that space, they would realise it is not quite so straightforward either.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: But we are mindful that, for a number of families, this is a serious issue, and we are looking at whether there are better ways to support them.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: It is also important for us to surface problems earlier so that we are able to step in, because a range of assistance schemes is available to help families, rather than let them try and figure out solutions on their own, incurring more debt and, thereby, creating much more complex problems for themselves.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: So, this is where the community needs to step in to support them, surface the problems, so that we can step in and see what we can do, early on.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We need to try new methods because social safety nets also need to evolve with changing conditions.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: So, I am keen for us to be as proactive as we can to go upstream to pre-empt issues.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: At the same time, it is also important to reiterate that we have to strike a balance in terms of being resilient and preventing a sense of entitlement.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Because by being so proactive, before you surface a problem, you come in and help somebody.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: I am not sure that is always a wise thing to do either.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: So, it is a balance that we need to strike, but I am very mindful that I would like to look at prevention as far as I can.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Prof Michael Sherradan, a distinguished professor of social development at the Washington University in St Louis in the US, described Singapore as "a relatively young and very tiny nation, but it has some of the most innovative social policies in the world".

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: He has also said that "social policies can never be perfect − trade-offs are always involved − but overall Singapore has made thoughtful and effective choices." I actually believe we can do better, especially in the way we provide more seamless and holistic help to individuals and families.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: When you meet individuals, they have a range of different problems and it is multi-dimensional.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: They do not organise their lives according to the way we organise ourselves in the Ministries and agencies.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: So, we, at the backend, need to see how to wrap around services to support them.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: For those with multi-faceted needs and challenges, clearly, financial assistance is just one part of the solution.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: So, as mentioned earlier, I think we can do better in trying to make this as seamless as possible.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: If you have one individual who is able to do everything, it will be challenging, because I do not think he will have that level of competency.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: So, you do need to leverage on the experts that are providing those services within the community.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: But what we can do is to link them up much better.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Basically, it is a team attending to the individual − but how do you help them navigate and how do you hand them over from one individual to the other and, collectively, try to address these issues?

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: I think that can go a very long way and that is something we can do better.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: These individuals and families are already having a lot of emotional stress, a lot of concerns on their minds and then they have to approach multiple agencies for help, and to repeat their stories.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: So, having technology to help streamline that so that there is a common database will help to go a very long way to prevent social workers from asking the individuals to repeat some of these instances.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: These experiences, we know, can be demoralising and can diminish their will to follow through with their action plans.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: In the first place, for many, I would suggest do have a great deal of dignity and self-reliance, which is why sometimes they actually come to us rather late.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Also, the processes at the backend, I think we can do better and we will.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: So, we will constantly explore better ways to be more client-centric.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: One area of focus, to illustrate, is employment assistance to enable job stability.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Some of our SSOs are co-located with WSG or e2i Career Centres, and clients can immediately follow up with WSG or e2i for employment assistance.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: At these two SSOs, the same SSO officer provides both social and employment assistance, an arrangement that clients have found helpful.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: For clients who are unemployed but able to work, this will provide easier and quicker access to employment assistance.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: They can also get more holistic help with employment goals tied closely to social assistance.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Much as we want to help, individuals must walk that last mile themselves.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Many of us who have been in this field, working with individuals, we will also meet individuals that, for one reason or other, somehow, are not prepared to embark on that.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: How do we nudge them on that journey, especially when they are work-capable?

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: So, we will train our officers to provide employment assistance.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: This is just one example, amongst various others, that we will need to continue to pursue to make sure that we can provide help as effectively as possible but also in a manner that helps the individual retain his dignity and, at the same time, not to erode the importance of self-reliance and also to include the families because family support remains important and, again, the community, which is where we are in.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We have also a responsibility in our local community to look out for our neighbours and our residents.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: There are many different ideas and schemes that can actually work on the ground, and many of us have tried that.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: The Enabling Masterplans are five-year blueprints that guide the development of policies, programmes and support services.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: The third Enabling Masterplan Steering Committee concluded their work in 2016.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: They seek to improve the quality of lives of persons with disabilities, importantly, to support caregivers and also to build up the community's capabilities and chart the way forward in building a more inclusive society.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: The third Masterplan builds on the progress of earlier Masterplans.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Focus group discussions were carried out with many stakeholders − persons with disabilities, caregivers, VWOs providing disability services, employers and members of the public.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: The recommendations highlight the importance of building an ecosystem of support for persons with disabilities.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: This ecosystem starts with family members and encompasses the larger community, such as health, education and social services and the society at large.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We will focus on strengthening this ecosystem to enable more holistic help and a smoother transition for persons with disabilities at different stages of their lives.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: I will also touch on the plans to build the community's capabilities to better support persons with disabilities and their families.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Early intervention will remain a key area of focus for children with developmental needs.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Timely and appropriate support in the early years can maximise their potential.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: The Developmental Support Programme (DSP) provides learning support and therapy for children with mild developmental delays, such as speech and language learning difficulties and behavioural issues.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: The programme is available in the mainstream preschools.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We are also studying how it can be enhanced to support children with moderate developmental needs.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We will build up the capability and capacity of the preschool sector.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: This includes training a pool of 200 preschool teachers called Learning Support Educators or LSEds, over the next five years.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: LSEds provide targeted intervention for children with mild developmental needs and they support classroom teachers in integrating these children with typically developing children in a group setting.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We will also promote greater inclusiveness within the educational setting.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: So, we are looking at the feasibility of an inclusive preschool model that enables special needs children to attend preschool with other children.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Such a model will need to be supported by LSEds and early intervention teachers.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We are keen on earlier detection and clearer classification of developmental needs to facilitate timely and appropriate intervention.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: In Singapore, this is something that we can do.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Personnel in the health and preschool sectors, they actually form a network of early touchpoints for our children.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: These include doctors and family medical practitioners as well as preschool teachers.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We will work with MOH to see how to better train these personnel to pick up signs of developmental delay and also to raise awareness and to deliberately look out for some of these indicators so that the children can be noticed at the early stage.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: And where it is appropriate, they can be referred for early and quicker intervention and appropriate support.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: The earlier the intervention, especially for those with issues, the better it is.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Children with special educational needs (SEN) who are able to benefit from formal education will be supported to access mainstream or Government-funded Special Education (SPED) schools.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Employment is integral to enabling persons with disabilities to live independently and integrate with society.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: It is something that also weighs on the minds of all parents with children with disabilities.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We share Ms Denise Phua's and Mr Desmond Choo's concerns on employment opportunities.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We will continue to do more to improve employability and employment options and support the acquisition of relevant skills.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: SG Enable has also supported internships for about 80 tertiary students with disabilities in our Institutes of Higher Learning.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: MSF, together with MOE and SG Enable, has piloted the School-to-Work Transition Programme with five SPED schools in 2014.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: This programme provides counselling, motivation, soft skills training and work trial opportunities for SPED students before they are matched for employment.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Training and lifelong learning are also crucial for persons with disabilities to keep current and relevant in this changing economy.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: It is challenging for us, but more challenging for those with disabilities.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Since 2014, more than 1,400 persons with disabilities have enrolled in training courses and more than 2,200 employers and co-workers have undergone training to learn how to recruit and integrate persons with disabilities at their workplace.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Mr Shahidir was diagnosed with mild autism at a young age and has difficulty in verbal communications.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Following a vocational assessment at Autism Resource Centre (ARC)'s Employability and Employment Centre in 2015, he was trained in work-related hard and soft skills.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: His job coach recognised his strengths in reading and ability to follow visual instructions, and matched him to an administrative role in DataPost Pte Ltd in April last year.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: His employer has been pleased with his consistent work performance so far.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Shahidir, like many of his peers, are assisted through job placement and job support services by SG Enable and its partners, and managed to become independent through employment.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: SG Enable will work with training providers to enhance the availability and affordability of training.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Persons with disabilities are now able to use their Post-Secondary Education Account (PSEA), in addition to SkillsFuture Credits, to offset costs across a wider range of courses, such as those offered by SG Enable.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Persons with disabilities can also tap on other schemes to enhance their independence, such as the Assistive Technology Fund (ATF).

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: This was introduced in 2003 to defray the cost of assistive technology devices.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We raised the monthly household per capita income from $1,500 to $1,800.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Persons with disabilities can now use ATF to purchase devices for rehabilitation or for assistance in daily living, in addition to work and education purposes.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: With these changes, the number of supported ATF applications went up from 175 in 2014 to about 1,600 in 2016.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: For those who still face difficulties in financing their purchases, our VWOs will work with them on a case-to-case basis.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We will monitor the needs of persons with disabilities and consider further enhancements in future.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Mr Faisal Manap suggested to keep prices affordable by aggregating demand.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: I think that is a useful idea; we will study the matter further as many AT devices are used by persons with disabilities.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: While some are standard, some actually do require customisation as well.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Sometimes, bulk purchases may not be quite so applicable.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: But this is something worth pursuing and we will study it.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Ms Thanaletchimi asked about wage support for companies employing persons with disabilities.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: The Special Employment Credit (SEC) scheme was introduced in 2012 to support companies that employ persons with disabilities earning $4,000 and below a month.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: These employers receive support of up to 16% of employees' wages, capped at $240.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: For persons with disabilities in low-wage jobs, the Wage Income Supplement (WIS) scheme further supplements their income and savings through cash payments and CPF in Workfare.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Twenty-eight million dollars in WIS has supplemented persons with disabilities' salaries in low-wage jobs.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Some special needs children graduating from the education system might not be able to enter employment, and they require longer term care services.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: For older adults with disabilities, their elderly parents who are their primary caregivers may find it harder to continue to care for them.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: So, a gap in caregiving may also be more keenly felt.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: As I have mentioned earlier, our families are becoming smaller.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: The role of a caregiver is physically and emotionally demanding and they can really be at risk of burn-out.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: I do note Ms Denise Phua's point about the need to be clear about the needs in the sector.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We will work with various stakeholders to tap on their experience in this particular space.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: This network will enable better access to information and resources, services, such as respite care, and capability-building resources, so that caregivers can perform their role with greater confidence.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: This is important because, sometimes, the stress comes from a lack of awareness.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: They feel that they may not be getting the support they need when, actually, some of these measures are available.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: A lot of it is about improving training and providing awareness.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: The greater the awareness, the lower the uncertainty.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: So, this is something that we will help to ensure – that information and resources are made available to families.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: This will also enable caregivers to, more importantly, be able to care for themselves, even as they care for their loved ones.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: VWOs and Family Service Centres in this network will help to link caregivers for further assistance based on their needs.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Caregivers will also have access to support groups that offer emotional support.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: VWOs will also provide caregivers access and connectivity with specialised services, such as counselling and specialised training.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Ms Chia Yong Yong has asked about this.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: The Centre will focus on new caregivers or caregivers of persons with disabilities who are currently not accessing services.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Adopting a "Hub and Spoke" model, the Centre will link these caregivers to VWO service providers in their community and other resources.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: The centre will also explore new support initiatives needed by caregivers.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We agree with Ms Denise Phua that this network has to be forward-looking.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: NCSS will ensure the Centre stays open to incorporating new care-giving ideas, innovation and practices.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: In order to make sure that it is forward-looking and it remains innovative, we ask stakeholders in the community to step forward and provide us some of these inputs and to work closely with NCSS on this front.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: One foremost concern by caregivers is what would happen to their child with special needs when they no longer are able to care for them.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: SNTC will also collaborate with key community partners, such as the Institute of Financial Literacy, in their outreach efforts.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Earlier, Ms Denise Phua touched on the range of residential living options for persons with disabilities.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: The family, as I mentioned, is the first line of support.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: The majority of persons with disabilities today are living with their family members.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Some are supported by home-based or community-based services.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: For those whose only option is to stay in residential care facilities due to high support needs, the Adult Disability Homes provide them with the required care and support.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: My Ministry will continue working with stakeholders to expand the continuum of support for persons with disabilities living in different residential settings.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Together with MOH, we will explore synergies across the health and social services.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: This would require collaboration amongst VWOs in areas of manpower training and transition management.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: I would say that one part that all of us can play is really in the community because persons with disabilities live amongst us.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: This is where, I think, the community can play a very active role, whether in terms of volunteers, whether in terms of the local neighbourhood, because we are there in the community with them.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We would urge that, even as we look at NCSS' initiatives, we look at the Government, the VWOs, I would remind us that, apart from the family, the community plays a very big part.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We can go a very long way in terms of providing support and respite for caregivers.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: When they are out and about in the community, you see them.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: But when we are less than sympathetic, when their children act up, when we are less empathetic, and we react in ways that are insensitive, it does not help at all.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: It makes them retreat into their own shell.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: They dare not come out; they are reluctant to come out.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: But the more we are able to actively involve them on a day-to-day basis in our community activities, let us deliberately plan for it, bring them out.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: If we are able to provide some form of care for their children or their family members, at least a couple of hours, half a day here or there, that can go a very long way in terms of making a real difference.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: That is something all of us can do.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We do not need to mandate that from the agencies.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: That is for us, as leaders in the community; that is something we can do.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: And we should think about how to embark on it.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: VWOs providing disability services would be able to reap the benefits of having a holistic view of clients and timely delivery of services enabled through technology.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Just as we embark on Smart Nation initiatives, the Smart Nation initiatives must be all-encompassing in every facet of our lives; no difference in this space as well.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Studies have also shown that Singaporeans are unsure about the appropriate behaviour when interacting with persons with disabilities.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: As I mentioned earlier, the more we are able to interact, the more we are consciously able to learn, the more we are able to be empathetic.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: This is one reason that employers are still apprehensive in hiring persons with disabilities.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: There are many little things that we can do to start creating greater inclusiveness.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Employers, for example, can look at designing more inclusive workplaces.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Our schools and communal places are natural settings, as I mentioned.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Of course, we can bridge that gap as well.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: But as much as we create the opportunities, again, for the rest of us, we must take that step.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: There are limits to how much we can force this down all our throats.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We create the opportunities, create the platforms but we must step forward and be there, be present, be involved.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Those who have been involved have found it enlightening.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: They began to have greater insights and that is the start of that journey.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: I think we are progressing but surveys show that we still have a long way to go.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: There is every possibility that we can make good improvements on this front.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: While I have elaborated on the upcoming new initiatives under the Enabling Masterplan, I think it is important for us to note that the on-going support for persons with disabilities range from early intervention, special education, wage support to supporting caregivers.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: And it straddles across many, many different Ministries and agencies as well.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Together, the key thing for us is to make sure that these schemes are able to come together, are able to be interwoven effectively to enable the holistic support to be provided.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: As a society, we all must subscribe to that, rather than to just turn to the Government, agencies, VWOs, and ask: what are you doing about it?

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Because all of us can play a part.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We need to be more aware, we need to remind ourselves, ask ourselves what role we can play to be more inclusive towards persons who have more needs than us, or whose capabilities differ from ours.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: It is our people that make this country special, and inclusiveness for the less fortunate amongst us should be an abiding value of our society.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: I hope that we remember that even as we provide initiatives to help those who are disabled, those who have special needs, those who are disadvantaged, really, it is not just about helping them.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: In the process, it is about us helping ourselves change.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Because when we participate in the process, that is the change that will happen.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: I do urge all of us, that, in this effort to build an inclusive society, it is not just about coming up with the schemes, it is not just throwing money at the problem, building infrastructure.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: And that is something all of us can do.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: (In Malay):   Sir, strengthening families has always been a key priority of my Ministry.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Over the past few years, my Ministry has implemented several broad measures to strengthen families.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We will continue to support families across life stages, from pre-marriage to new parenthood and the challenging teenage years.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: For instance, we have enhanced paternity leave and introduced the Child Development Account (CDA) First Step for all parents.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: In order to support this increase in infant care and childcare places, we will enhance our efforts to attract more workers to this important sector.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We will pilot a new approach to training, to attract capable and experienced individuals to take care of infants.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We will also improve career prospects and professional development in the early childhood sector.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We will also provide targeted support for children from needy families.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This is to ensure that they also receive quality early childhood development support.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Under this pilot programme, we worked with the Social Service Offices, Family Service Centres, hospitals and community partners that manage the KidSTART programme.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We identified, reached out to and then provided holistic support to these children and families.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: For instance, KidSTART home visitors regularly visit parents who have infants at home to share knowledge and skills about the child's growth, health and nutrition.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: One of the families that benefited from this pilot programme is the family of Mdm Azlinah Binte Jumali.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Two of her children attend a childcare centre and her youngest child is waiting to enrol in infant care.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Under the KidSTART programme, she has learnt more about early childhood development issues.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This initiative had a positive impact on her children's development and her family's well-being.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Although we are still in the midst of rolling out this pilot programme, we are encouraged by its positive impact on the interaction and relationship between parents and their children so far.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Families are the basic building blocks of society and key pillars of support for individuals.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We want to make Singapore a great place to raise children and build families.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We will do all we can to continue to support families through significant milestones and life-stages, especially those who need help to stay together and strong.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: (In English): Strengthening families has always been a key priority of my Ministry.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Families are the basic building blocks of society and key pillars of support for individuals.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We want Singapore to be a great place to raise children and build families.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We will do all we can to continue to support families through significant milestones and life-stages, especially those who need help to stay together and strong.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We want every child to have a good start in life and grow to become caring, resilient and engaged individuals in society.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: To realise these aspirations, my Ministry has undertaken various initiatives in recent years.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We have introduced broad-based measures that support families across life stages, from pre-marriage to new parenthood and the challenging teenage years.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We have enhanced paternity leave and introduced the Child Development Account (CDA) First Step.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We have also extended Government-Paid Maternity Leave and the CDA benefits to unwed mothers.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Since 2012, the number of childcare places has increased by more than 40% to about 140,000 places today.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We have also enhanced means-tested childcare and kindergarten subsidies.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Since 2012, the number of beneficiaries from these means-tested subsidies has doubled to about 45,000 children.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: To support low-income and vulnerable children, we have piloted the KidSTART and Safe and Strong Families initiatives, which I will talk more about later.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This year, we will continue efforts to build strong families, support parenthood and ensure a good start for every child.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We will provide comprehensive support for families who experience abuse and neglect.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Ms Jessica Tan asked about the measures to support parents and build stronger family relationships.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We believe that building strong family relationships should be supported from the very start.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Children grow well when they are raised in a close-knit family.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Hence, we work with community partners to provide marriage preparation programmes, covering communication, problem-solving and conflict resolution between couples.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Parenting skills have to evolve as children become tweens and teens.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Under the FamilyMatters! initiative, we piloted the Positive Parenting Programme (Triple P) and signposts in schools to support parents during their children's transition years.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Partnerships with the community are critical in rejuvenating and reinforcing family ties.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We work with family champions, such as the Families for Life Council and the Centre for Fathering, to reach out to families.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Last year, the Registry of Marriages sent commemorative certificates to couples celebrating their 55th anniversary.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Families for Life also organises meaningful and celebratory programmes, such as the 2017 Marriage Convention, for couples to reaffirm their lifelong commitment.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Mr Kok Heng Leun and Mr Desmond Choo asked about the support for single-parent families.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Over the years, we have reviewed and introduced new programmes to better support children from families with single parents, who may be divorced, widowed or unwed.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Today, we already extend benefits that support children's growth and development to all children, regardless of their parents' marital status.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Single parents in need of financial and socio-emotional support can also approach our Social Service Offices and Family Service Centres.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We have stepped up support for divorced and widowed single parents, who form the bulk of single-parent families.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: In our housing policies, divorced and widowed parents with children are recognised as a family nucleus, similar to married parents.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: HDB's Assistance Scheme for Second-Timers (ASSIST) also gives priority to divorced and widowed parents.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: As our policies may not address every circumstance, HDB exercises flexibility to help single parents with their housing needs on a case-by-case basis.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Mr Kok asked if we could do away with the use of "illegitimacy" in inheritance and tax reliefs.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This suggestion has far reaching implications and will need careful consideration.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Our society continues to desire parenthood within marriages and we should promote it.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Mr Leon Perera spoke about the role of the Government in collecting maintenance payments.
