speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Maintenance of children as well as spouses and ex-spouses is, first and foremost, a family responsibility.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: A collection agency may not guarantee that claimants receive maintenance, if it is unable to obtain payment from the other party.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: There is thus a need to differentiate between those who can afford but refuse to pay maintenance, from those who are genuinely unable to pay.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Concurrently, the referral system to the Social Service Offices has been enhanced, to help families and individuals in financial need if they are identified.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We will continue to explore ways to make our enforcement regime more effective and robust, without eroding the principle of family responsibility.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Given the ramp-up in childcare places, we have already exceeded our 2017 target of providing one place for every two children.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We agree with Er Dr Lee Bee Wah that there is still unmet demand in estates with more young families.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: At the Second Reading of the Early Childhood Development Centres Bill, Ms Joan Pereira also suggested building childcare centres and HDB flats concurrently.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: They will work with HDB to bring forward the completion of childcare centres for new Build-To-Order (BTO) developments as much as possible.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Mr Ang Hin Kee asked about our plans to expand infant and childcare services.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Many of these new places will be in new housing areas, such as Punggol, Sengkang, Tampines, Woodlands and Yishun.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Overall, parents now have more options for affordable and quality childcare.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Almost half of all the preschool children are enrolled in an Anchor or Partner Operator centre where fees are capped.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Mr Louis Ng also asked for childcare to be made more affordable for stay-at-home mothers.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We do see more working mothers requiring full-day childcare services to help manage their work and care-giving responsibilities.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: For non-working mothers, they can choose to place their children in shorter kindergarten programmes that focus more on child development.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: These are generally more affordable, with a median monthly fee of $170 compared to around $850 for childcare before subsidies.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Regardless of the mother's working status, low- and middle income children enrolled in Anchor Operator or MOE kindergartens receive further support with the Kindergarten Fee Assistance Scheme (KiFAS).

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: With KiFAS, a low-income family can pay as little as $1 a month for preschool.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We will continue to pay close attention to the cost of raising children and regularly review the affordability of preschool.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: While we continue to improve centre-based infant and childcare, we acknowledge that some parents may prefer to have their children cared for at home, as mentioned by Miss Cheryl Chan and Mr Gan Thiam Poh.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: It is not feasible to extend centre-based grants to home-based care.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: While our centres are governed by regulations to ensure quality and service standards, home-based care is more informal and based on mutual trust and support.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: As home-based care is varied in nature, it is impractical to apply common standards.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Also, while we recognise the contributions of these home caregivers, we must be careful not to monetise personal relationships.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Nevertheless, we have been progressively enhancing parental leave schemes to support parents who prefer home-based care.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Parents can also tap on the CDA First Step to help defray approved child-related expenses.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah, Assoc Prof Randolph Tan, Mr Ang Hin Kee and Ms Jessica Tan mentioned the need to increase the supply, salaries and capability of educators to support the expansion of early childhood services.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Our work with operators and training agencies to attract, retain and develop early childhood educators has started to bear fruit.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Salaries have been rising steadily across all job roles − salaries of entry-level diploma trained teachers are competitive and comparable to other sectors.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: To further support these efforts, my Minister launched the Early Childhood Manpower Plan last October to provide professional development opportunities, better recognition and a more supportive working environment for early childhood educators.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Even as we attract fresh school leavers, the early childhood sector offers meaningful and attractive careers for mid-career workers who want to switch sectors and women wanting to re-join the workforce.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: These Allied Infant Educarers will work with existing infant care staff to provide holistic care and development for infants aged two to 18 months.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: To train Allied Infant Educarers, we will also pilot a new training approach.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We understand that some people with the interest, aptitude and competence to care for infants may be unable to join the sector, either because they do not want to attend classroom-based training, or they lack the appropriate academic records.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Under this pilot, ECDA will work with the SEED Institute and Anchor Operators to provide new entrants with on-the-job training and coaching to work as Allied Infant Educarers.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Our emphasis will be on aptitude and competency, rather than academic qualifications.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This is in line with Mr Ang Hin Kee's suggestion to look into allied job roles.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Training for the first batch of Allied Infant Educarers will begin later this month.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: With the Allied Infant Educarers supporting our existing infant educarers, the more experienced ones can then progress to become Senior Infant Educarers.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: These Senior Infant Educarers will receive training to coach and mentor new entrants.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Some will play a more active role in facilitating developmental activities for our infants.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Overall, parents can feel assured that their infants will benefit from higher-quality infant care.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Ms Nyaneswari d/o Paramasivam is a mother of two.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: She previously worked as an untrained staff at a childcare centre but, more recently, worked in other jobs in security, administration and after-school care.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: With this new opportunity to become an Allied Infant Educarer, she has decided to come back to the sector.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Ms Nyaneswari welcomes the new training approach with more hands-on practice.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This is similar to how she learnt to care for her own children; by observing how her mother cared for her and her siblings.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We need more individuals like her to join this meaningful profession.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Mr Ang Hin Kee and Ms Jessica Tan rightly highlighted the need to ensure quality, even as we scale up these early childhood services.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The Early Childhood Development Centres Bill recently passed in Parliament is one initiative to raise and ensure consistent quality standards across the sector.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: To enhance quality in the sector, we will provide more structured professional and career development opportunities for our educators.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Today, I am happy to announce that we will be launching the Professional Development Programme (PDP) for Educarers this month.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Educarers are early childhood professionals who work with infants, toddlers and nursery-age children.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Similar to an earlier PDP for preschool teachers, educarers will undergo a structured training over three years to deepen their skills and prepare them for larger job roles, such as team leaders and mentors to newer colleagues.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Overall, our approach towards raising the quality and professionalism in the early childhood sector is aligned with the SkillsFuture movement.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Early childhood educators should be provided opportunities to deepen competencies throughout their career.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Last year, ECDA launched the Skills Framework for the early childhood sector to map out career pathways and competencies for various job roles.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: With this Advanced Diploma, teachers will be better prepared to take on larger roles, such as lead teachers and curriculum specialists, and thereby raise the quality of our preschools.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We recognise that low-income and vulnerable children will need more support to get a good start in life.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Mr Louis Ng asked whether we could strengthen the Kindergarten Fee Assistance Scheme (KiFAS) to improve the attendance of preschoolers in kindergartens.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: He has rightly highlighted that the reasons behind irregular preschool attendance are not so straightforward.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: There are many other needs of the child, such as health, social skills and emotional development.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This is why we introduced the KidSTART pilot last year to proactively identify and support these children in their early years.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: As part of the programme, KidSTART home visitors regularly visit parents and their infants.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: They support parents with practical skills and knowledge for the child's growth, health and nutrition.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: These home visitors also work closely with social service agencies, such as Family Service Centres, to address the multiple challenges faced by some of these parents.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Any success under KidSTART depends on close partnerships with the community.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Ms Nur Azlinah Binte Jumali is a mother of four, with two children in childcare and the youngest waiting to enrol in infant care.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Under KidSTART, she learnt more about early childhood development issues from professionals, socialised with other mothers in the community and received help for her children's necessities.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: These have improved the children's development and her family's well-being.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We hope that KidSTART can continue to create such success stories.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We are also piloting an enhanced support model at preschools.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Today, 10 Anchor Operator centres are provided additional manpower to better engage parents of children from low-income and vulnerable families enrolled at these centres.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: These Child Enabling Executives closely monitor the children's developmental needs and improve their school attendance.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We will need to review and refine our processes before introducing KidSTART to more locations.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: In the near term, ECDA will partner the community to roll out more playgroups and enhance support for preschools in the pilot areas.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We believe that children grow best in families where they can bond with familiar persons who can help them develop socially and emotionally.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Unfortunately, there are times when a child cannot be safe in his family because of abuse and neglect.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: In such times, my Ministry believes in empowering these families to provide proper and safe care for the child where possible.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: If this is not feasible, the child should be cared for in a nurturing foster family, where available, until we are able to reunite them safely with their natural families.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: To better care for abused, neglected children, my Ministry began efforts to transform the out-of-home care sector in 2013.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The emphasis is on creating more options for family-based care by growing fostering capacity and providing intensive support to keep children with their families.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: My Ministry has been expanding our fostering capacity by stepping up outreach and setting up two fostering agencies.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We plan to set up a third fostering agency later in the year.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We previously aimed to recruit 500 foster families by 2019.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This achievement is very encouraging and I would like to thank these warm-hearted foster parents for opening their hearts and homes to vulnerable children who need love and care.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Last year, my Ministry celebrated the 60th anniversary of the Fostering Scheme and published a commemorative book.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: One of my favourite stories is that of Mr Tan Kah Poh and his wife, Mdm Chua Siew Gek.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: When their first foster child came to them, he was traumatised and anxious.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Through their daily care and nurturing, the foster child is now well-adjusted.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The couple have even taken in a second foster child.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: I hear that the foster children like their delicious chicken rice and this was the secret to their "chemistry".

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We often take simple family meals for granted.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Yet, as shown in this story, these little family rituals make such a positive difference to our children.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: While we encourage fostering, it would be even better if more natural families can care safely for their own children and not require out-of-home care at all.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Many caregivers who come to our attention through the child welfare system do want to care for their children.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: With additional support and links to resources, it is possible for them to learn how to provide better and safer care for their children.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Hence, MSF announced the Safe and Strong Families (SSF) pilot last year.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The pilot aims to preserve the care of children within their families and reunify children who were temporarily removed, back with their families when conditions are safe and stable.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Under SSF, professionals work intensively with parents at home to rebuild their relationships with their children and learn how to care for them safely.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Ms Jessica Tan asked for an update on the SSF pilot.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin asked whether national surveys could be conducted to understand youth well-being and improve interventions for youths-at-risk.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Today, many agencies already do so, to better understand our youth trends and concerns.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: These include the Student Health Survey by the Health Promotion Board, the National Youth Survey by the National Youth Council as well as the Youth Perception Survey by the National Council Against Drug Abuse.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: One key programme that has yielded positive results is the Youth GO!

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Programme which was launched in 2012 to reach out to at-risk youths on the streets.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Under this programme, social and youth workers keep a look out for youths on the streets who may be at risk and befriend them over multiple sessions to better understand their situation as well as build trust.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: During these sessions, the Youth GO! workers also help youths who may be experiencing trouble in school or with peers and family, and work closely with them to resolve or cope with these issues better.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Early findings showed that youths engaged under the Youth GO!

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Programme displayed a positive change in attitude towards their parents, studies and career plans.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Mr Amrin Amin asked a timely question about our plans to strengthen family relationships and prevent escalation to family violence.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: While the number of reported family violence cases is low and stable, every case is of concern to us.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Furthermore, family violence is often a hidden problem and cases may go unreported.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We have completed a study to understand public perceptions on family violence.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Findings showed that awareness about family violence remains low.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: In addition, children were less likely to seek help compared to adults.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We need to go upstream and educate all segments of our society that strong, positive relationships are the best way to prevent escalation of family violence.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We will focus on family violence prevention strategies targeted at different stages of a person's life.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: For the young, we will continue to cultivate understanding about respectful relationships in schools.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: In Character and Citizenship Education, students learn how to develop positive relationships with their family members, manage family conflicts effectively and seek help when the situation calls for it.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: For couples who intend to get married, we have worked with community partners to enhance marriage preparation courses to emphasise respectful relationships.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: It just takes a small act to prevent the escalation of family violence.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Family violence is unacceptable and should not be allowed to perpetuate.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We should continue to encourage those affected by family violence to seek assistance and urge the community to play their part by reporting abuse immediately.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Let us "Break the Silence" against family violence.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: There are two key principles under the Vulnerable Adults Act.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: If the vulnerable adult has to be removed from the place where he is staying, MSF will explore if he or she can be placed with any suitable relatives.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We will also work with community agencies, such as Social Service Offices and Family Service Centres, to provide additional support.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: If community and family options are not feasible, MSF will be empowered to place the vulnerable adult at gazetted places of temporary care and protection and places of safety.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Ms Rahayu Mahzam also asked about the progress of the Mental Capacity Act which was amended last year.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We are developing the framework for the professional deputy and donee scheme.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: When the scheme is launched at the end of this year, professionals, such as lawyers, accountants, social workers, doctors and nurses, may register to be professional deputies or donees.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Miss Cheryl Chan asked whether the Government is working with the community to provide home-based care options for the elderly, many of whom prefer to age in their homes with their loved ones for as long as they can.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: In addition to programmes by MOH, MSF also has Senior Cluster Networks to coordinate and integrate services for vulnerable seniors living in rental flats, within each town.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The Networks reach out to low-income and vulnerable seniors living alone so that they can age within the community.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: In addition to that, we have the Smart Elderly Monitoring and Alert System (SEMAS) which is piloted by HDB in Yuhua and this will provide another form of support to our seniors.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: However, there is much more that goes into enabling and sustaining strong families.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Relationships will only grow stronger if we invest the necessary time and effort in building them.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We can encourage them to invest quality-time with their spouses and families, resolve their issues amicably and seek professional help when needed.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: MSF and the National Council of Social Service (NCSS) have worked steadily with partners on a number of fronts.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We also expanded professional hubs for therapists and started one for psychologists.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: In the areas of manpower development and skills upgrading, the Social Service Institute under NCSS has expanded its range of courses and learning platforms and, today, offers close to 700 courses for social sector leaders, professionals and volunteers.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We enhanced career development opportunities in the sector.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: And this helps retain our professionals and attract more to join the sector.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh asked about improving wages for social workers.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: NCSS publishes salary guidelines for the social service sector and these are updated every year to ensure salaries keep pace with wage movements in the market.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Every three years, there is a major review of salary benchmarks for the different professions.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: In between the major reviews, there are salary guidelines that incorporate a recommended salary increment.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: To ensure that the salaries remain competitive, the benchmarks are pegged to professions in the main competing markets, for example, the healthcare and public sectors.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: The salary guidelines for social workers take reference from those in the Civil Service.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: As we all know, beyond salaries, other factors contribute to retention.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: NCSS launched the People Practice Consultancy last year to help VWOs improve their human resource practices.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: These efforts at the organisational level continue to be important.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Well-run organisations are better able to retain their professionals and provide better service to their clients as well.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: While we have made progress on some fronts, the sector faces certain challenges going forward, such as – and we are all familiar with them − an ageing workforce, slower workforce growth and increasing complexity of demands.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: These challenges raise questions on whether our service models are sustainable and whether our skills will remain relevant in future.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We also need to prepare our workforce for these challenges.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Achieving our vision of a caring Singapore in this environment requires all of us to play a role.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: The three key groups are the VWOs; secondly, the social service workforce, and lastly, volunteers.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: There are over 450 VWOs registered as members of NCSS.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: They ensure that social services are able to meet clients' needs even as resources get leaner.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Mr Png Eng Huat asked how we are helping and funding VWOs, especially the smaller ones.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: MSF and NCSS have been supporting VWOs in strengthening their organisational capabilities, so that they can be more effective.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: The VWOs-Charities Capability Fund, or VCF, was started in 2002 to support these initiatives.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Through the VCF, VWOs can grow and they can develop their organisations.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Ms K Thanaletchmi asked if the VCF could be directed towards talent attraction and retention.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: This is done through the Professional Capability Grant.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: VWOs can apply for subsidies for their staff to undergo local or overseas training, upgrade their professional qualifications and introduce supervision frameworks for professional development.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: With stronger skills, they can make better progress in their careers and take on larger job roles.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: The Organisational Development Grant supports VWOs in improving their effectiveness as organisations.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: VWOs can engage consultants to help them in strategy development, as well as review and improve internal work processes, such as HR practices and service delivery.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: The Innovation and Productivity Grant helps build a culture of continuous improvement.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: It funds applied research that leads to improved services and productivity gains.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: These include IT systems and other efforts to make better use of resources.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: All these grants are open to all NCSS members regardless of their size.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: NCSS has enhanced its website over the past year to improve the availability and clarity of information on the VCF.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: It will also be sharing information on past projects supported by the VCF on its website, so that VWOs can consider relevant ideas or collaborate with one another.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: The Association for Persons with Special Needs, or APSN, tapped on the VCF Innovation and Productivity Grant to develop a Student Management System.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: This would automate previously manual tasks, such as class and academic management, at the Special Needs Schools and Centres that it runs.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: The first phase of the system was implemented last year.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: With the system, teachers now have more time for teaching and supporting their students' learning and development.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: I encourage more VWOs to also make use of the available VCF resources to gear up for the future.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Ms Chia Yong Yong asked about support in project scoping and the use of consultants.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: For some key areas of capability building, NCSS will pre-select consultants to work with our VWOs.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We have care workers who tend to the daily needs of clients, professionals who deliver specialised interventions and executives who head the VWOs.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: All of them play critical roles in caring for the vulnerable in our society.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Some of you asked how we are developing them and improving their competencies.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: This framework will provide more information on the job opportunities available and the qualifications required.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: It will also inform social service professionals on the career development pathways and the skills required to perform the key jobs.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Professionals, such as social workers, psychologists, early intervention teachers, youth workers and care workers, will be able to use this to guide their growth in the sector.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We are also working with MOH in developing a Skills Framework for therapists.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: In 2015, the SkillsFuture Study Award was launched to enable Singaporeans with some working experience to deepen their skills in the social service and early childhood sectors.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Last year, we also launched the SkillsFuture Study Award for persons with disabilities and disability employment professionals.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Mr Amrin Amin and Ms Tin Pei Ling highlighted the important role that the community and volunteers play in complementing the work of our professionals.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: During the Budget debate, a number of Members talked about growing the community network of support.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Indeed, VWOs need to work with the members of the communities they serve for them to be effective.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Shafik was a Secondary 1 Normal (Technical) student at St Gabriel's Secondary School.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: His mother became the sole breadwinner, working two jobs to support Shafik and his three sisters.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: With the troubles he faced at home, his self-esteem was affected; he nose-dived.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: He was involved in bullying, fighting with other boys and even teachers.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Along the way, he was selected by his school for the ""Uth" Power!" Programme.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: This is a motivational support programme by CARE Singapore, a VWO, which aims to help at-risk students stay in school.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Derek, who is a CARE Singapore staff, reached out to Shafik and spent extra time with him after school.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Shafik refused to respond for more than a year, but eventually came around owing to Derek's fatherly presence and persistence and the continual support of the volunteers that supported this programme.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: After graduating, Shafik volunteered with CARE as often as possible.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: In 2010, he was employed by CARE as a youth support worker and continues to grow as a professional.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: He is aiming to complete his diploma in counselling in June this year.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: He is also planning to eventually obtain a degree and a masters in counselling.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: He has touched the lives of many students, first as a volunteer, then as a professional.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: His journey was made possible through the support of many members of the community, including those who played the role of volunteers.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: I strongly believe that as we care through volunteering, we are tending to the soul of the nation.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: It is in changing that we become better people.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: It is in having better people that we begin to become a more caring and inclusive society, a better society.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: That is why we must find ways to grow our community of support and encourage even more to volunteer.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: It is not just about helping the disadvantaged, the disabled, the elderly.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: It is very much about helping us all change.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: First of all, we can catalyse, support and publicise volunteering initiatives using Singapore Cares (SG Cares) as a platform.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: The Singapore Cares movement aims to involve more individuals to get them involved in building a compassionate and inclusive society.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Jointly coordinated by the National Volunteer and Philanthropy Centre (NVPC) and NCSS, Singapore Cares seeks to create an environment where we all feel empowered to make a difference.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We want to mobilise the community to meet real needs.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We can also help by fostering partnerships between corporates, non-profit organisations, schools and other partners.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: The biggest partners in this movement are the volunteers.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: By organising ourselves better, by sharing information and by enabling volunteers through training and effective use of technology, we can not only help more but help more effectively as well.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: It is really about more giving and volunteering by individuals and groups, and a lot of this is already taking place in the community.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: SG Cares provides an overall umbrella to encourage and support these efforts, to help and facilitate even more outreach.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: For one, we can help with training of volunteers.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Other e-learning courses will also be developed to equip volunteers to work with persons with disabilities, with the elderly, children with special needs and so on.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: NCSS is also working on an app to better match interested volunteers to opportunities at VWOs.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Many people want to help but are not sure where to go, what to do.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: With SG Cares, we aim to work with various community partners to facilitate collaboration.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: In our schools, we want to make volunteerism a way of life for all our children.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: For example, the WonderKids programme is a partnership between student leaders at Hai Sing Catholic School and the Pasir Ris Family Service Centre.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: As part of this programme, the students befriend and mentor children from lower income households.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Besides benefiting these children, Hai Sing students have also grown to have a deeper understanding of community needs.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: In the workplaces, we are helping corporates to partner with VWOs within the same neighbourhood, making it easier.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We want to facilitate long-term, meaningful partnerships to meet real needs in the local community.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: For example, the Singapore Power Group partnered TOUCH Senior Activity Centre in Geylang Bahru.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Located in close proximity, staff from Singapore Power Group are able to commit to regular visits to the Centre and accompany the elderly for their morning exercises and then prepare and serve them breakfast.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We would like to see more of such local partnerships leading to long-term and meaningful impact.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: At home in the community, we are working with community Advisors on how to grow a network on the ground.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We need stakeholders to come together, share information and coordinate.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: VWOs, GPs, childcare centres, merchants and other independent groups are examples of stakeholders who may be able to pick up early indicators of problems of people in need and then we are able to then match them with sources of help, to be more attractive and to be able to deal with it upstream.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Dr Lily Neo talked about recruiting volunteers to reach out to lonely seniors.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: MSF and MOH have been funding befriending programmes for seniors, such as the Caring Assistance from Neighbours, or the CAN programme, Befriending Service and the Community Befriending Programme.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Ageing, we all know, will be a significant feature of our landscape.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Without volunteers, it is very difficult for us to just depend on healthcare and social workers to deal with all the needs that we know will be facing us in the community in the years to come.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: As Members know, last year, ComChest launched the Share as One programme to encourage more individual giving and create more workplace giving and volunteering opportunities.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: In addition, more than 630 companies have increased their SHARE donations.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: These are improvements but, frankly, we really can and should do more.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Many companies are not on board but more of them can be.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Please do encourage them to come on board and we will do our part as well.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: In closing, let me highlight that our VWOs, social service workforce and volunteers collectively form the community that my Ministry and our partner agencies are working to empower, so that each can have a stronger and more lasting impact on society, particularly for those who are most in need.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: As Ms Tin Pei Ling has noted, values really lie at the heart of all we do.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Values, such as care and compassion, resilience, as well as strong and supportive families and communities, these will stand us in good stead as we face the various and many challenges that are looming ahead on the horizon.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We need the concerted effort and commitment of the people, private and public sectors to come together, to work hand-in-hand, to overcome these challenges.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Through the process, we will forge stronger bonds between the sectors, stronger communities, stronger families, more resilient individuals and we will create the bonds that will bind us as a society.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: That is the kind of resilience that we will need.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Together, we will build a more inclusive and caring society.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: It is really about enabling us to be not just compassionate, but to look at ourselves as a community.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: To not just look at "my own interests alone", but to look at "us" as a community, not just for the present but for the long term.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: That is where, perhaps, you deal with the issues of self-entitlement; that is also where we deal with the issues of sacrifice, where we deal with the issues of community.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Where there is a sense of that, that is where we can truly see that we have an inclusive society.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: That is when we can begin to build the best home possible for all Singaporeans.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: On one hand, the community can definitely play a role but, sometimes, the community cannot comprehensively identify these families whereas the Government, as a whole, may be able to identify them in a more effective manner, such as escalating arrears in HDB rent, utilities and, perhaps, even S&CC.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: I will leave it to my Parliamentary Secretary to take the second question on allied infant educarers.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: In terms of identifying problems early, there are many indicators in society.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: For example, we will arrears not just in Town Council, but arrears in terms of utility bills.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: You also sometimes pick up indicators from the local kindergartens, where we note certain families are having issues paying fees.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: This is something that we are looking at, how best to tap on information and data.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Partly, there is also information protection that we need to deal with across the different agencies.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: But we are also very mindful, as I mentioned earlier, if we are too proactive, because from time to time, individuals may have cash flow problems, they can deal with it.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We are quite clear that our agencies need to collaborate better at the backend.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: For example, we are picking indicators as one agency; another agency might be picking up another indictor within their realms of responsibility.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: When you put it all together, the picture begins to surface that certain families might be facing financial duress, for example.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: That is something that we are looking at, in terms of how do we facilitate the sharing of information that can better address some of these problems earlier.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: The other issue to me is the community which is why I think there are efforts that we can put in at the local level to pull in the different stakeholders.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We are living there, we are encountering the individuals in different capacities − whether they will be going to the local mosque, to the local church or the marketplace, at the hawker centres, or the GPs.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Sometimes, conversations may arise when the individuals are facing some stress.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: One, is to make sure that the information is available.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: They know where to go − they can look for the Advisor, they can look for the ComCare hotline or the SSO.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: The increase in numbers is not just because we have increased our coverage, but because it has become more accessible, a lot more awareness is beginning to arise amongst the public.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We see residents surfacing to us that their neighbours or their friends may be having some of these issues.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: The key is, when problems arise, individuals must know what is available.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We encourage them to step forward where they can.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: But that is where the community can also play a big part.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: At the backend, at the agencies, as I have said, what we can do better is between the agencies – watching that space, could we share the information a lot better?

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: This is something that we are working on.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We are mindful of confidentiality issues but we are trying to deal with that as well.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: But as I have said, as we are dealing with this, I am very mindful that we need to strike that balance − how intrusive you want us to be.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We can be very, very intrusive but I am not sure that is necessarily a wise way to deal with it.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: But the main thing is make sure information is available, people know where to go.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Please come forward to see us when help is needed.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: There are a few things that we will do.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We want to make sure that the right person becomes the mentor.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: There are milestones that need to be met so that the On-the-Job training (OJT) will be very meaningful and can replicate what is really out there.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We will work with the pilot centres and we will have visits and make sure that developmental and regulation kind of processes will be in place.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: With all these, I strongly believe it will help the educarers to focus on their job.

speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin
text: First, on the youth surveys, there is a very distinct difference between the questions that are currently asked in youth surveys and the kind of questions that the Icelandic researchers did.

speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin
text: So, I will request that the Ministry take a look at it.

speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin
text: But, anyway, I am thankful that you mentioned all those surveys.

speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin
text: My second request is about the single unwed mothers issue.

speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin
text: I understand the desire to protect the principle of encouraging childbirth in the context of marriage.

speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin
text: I personally stand by this principle and I believe it serves society well.

speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin
text: However, the Parliamentary Secretary mentioned just now that responsibility to the family is a critical guiding principle to protect in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin
text: So, in the case of unwed mums, are they not demonstrating responsibility to the family in their choice to keep and raise their child?

speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin
text: And if we say, "Yes, they are exercising responsibility to family", then are we not —

speaker: The Chairman
text: Ms Kuik, could you please put forward your clarification; you are making another speech.

speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin
text: So, are we saying then that we actually do define the unwed mother and child as family?

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: On the first question, we will take note of the Member's request.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: On the second question, as I have said, if we look at how our society has evolved, we have been making progress on this front.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Nevertheless, we will help, wherever possible, whoever we can, every Singaporean.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: I mentioned earlier that there are policies that cannot cover everything but we will look at issues on a case-by-case basis.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: I, personally, have seen my residents who may not come under certain policies, but they are being helped.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: At the end of the day, we want to make a difference to the lives of Singaporeans.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: Many of our residents want to have childcare centres near their home.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: The current provision is clearly not adequate because our residents have to send their children elsewhere.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: The 90-100 places per BTO is grossly inadequate.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: I would just like to seek clarification on the different components that he mentioned in his speech: in particular, what is the breakdown of the numbers of children that have been reached out to by the Ministry per component of the programme?

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We have three components: one is the home visitation; second, the KidSTART groups; the third is the KidSTART enhanced support to preschools.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: And it has been an enriching process, not only for the parents and children but for the people involved in KidSTART.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Again, I would like to encourage more Singaporeans to come forward to play a part in making a difference in the lives of our fellow Singaporeans, especially the needy ones.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: I just want to say that meaning and policies do affect the way people perceive things.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: And so, here, I hope you also would agree that the word "illegitimate" is actually quite negative.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: When you were saying that if we do away with the "illegitimate" issues on tax relief and inheritance issue, that would have a far-reaching impact.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: We must be able to justify this impact or else these kids are going to bear this stigma for the rest of their lives.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: It has to be how our society has evolved.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, as I have said earlier, it is something that we have to consider carefully.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We hear the different groups of people and we want to make sure that we journey on this together with our society.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: About the question on foreign spouses, as I have said, even though policies may not allow as such but, more importantly, if you know of anyone facing such an issue, ask them to see their Members of Parliament and we will see how we can facilitate that.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: I agree that community involvement is very important in society.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: I have raised in my question just now about the need to improve on the community engagement programmes for our students because they do spend a substantial number of hours contributing to community today.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: But I have also seen many cases because of the ineffective management of the programmes, we have kind of lost the interest of all these youths and, eventually, we could not bring them towards active volunteerism.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: I would suggest that it is not just schools but, I think, every platform, including corporates − doing it for corporate branding reason, corporate social responsibility motivation − notwithstanding that, if done well, it can have a transformative effect.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We have seen how it has happened for some, whether in schools or elsewhere.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: I have experienced the various Values-in-Action	(VIA) programmes.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Some, you know, connect emotionally with the children and you can see that even though children may do it compulsorily because they have to – they have got to clock up the hours, they want to enhance their CV – but, as a result of the experience, it changes them.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Which is why volunteering is not just about doing the thing, it is about changing lives.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: You can imagine the individual wanting to continue to give and to be involved, perhaps, for life.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Imagine if every child can leave the school system having some semblance of that.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: That is a vision that is worth working towards.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Well, I am sure it is difficult to get everyone to be converted that way.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: But I think it is possible because they are still in school, you have a captive audience.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: You can run and curate structured programmes where you are able to enable such learning to take place.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: It is not about forcing it down their throats but by making sure that their journey is meaningful.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: The school plays a very big part; I think how the school appoints the teachers.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: It is not just being arrowed to do that, but putting heart and mind into how do you educate the child in the process.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: My message is also to VWOs as well.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Your KPI cannot be just about people coming in, helping you and, therefore, doing the thing that you need to do to service your clients and to look after those you are looking after.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: But your responsibility is also to make sure that every volunteer that joins you believes in your cause and wants to come back.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: They do very much believe that values can be inculcated.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: The very term "Values-in-Action", I think it is a very apt term for the programme because values are realised in action.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We are working with them to see how to curate some of these experiences.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We know some schools have done a fantastic job − very good outcomes – and we would like to see more of this happening.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: But I would also suggest that not just for schools but even corporates and even other organisations that are looking at volunteering, I think we can pay attention to their journey as well.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi
text: With regard to VWOs, how integrated in terms of systems are they in the social sector so that the case management of individuals that come for help is well taken care of?

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi
text: The second question is, have you considered shared services for certain operational admin services which VWOs, about 400 of them, require in commonality?

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi
text: These shared services can bring down the so-called operational costs.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi
text: And the third question is: have we considered forming an association in the social sector for VWOs so that they can learn the best practices and even complement each other with the resources and exchange views?

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We have gatherings of the leaders and the various VWOs coming together; sometimes,there are focus areas of discussion.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: I have participated in some of these and they have been quite energising sessions.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: It serves to re-motivate many of them as well.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: They establish relationships and friendships, renew them and establish new ones which are very important in terms of collaboration work and, importantly, the exchange of good practices.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We can do more and we aim to work with the social work fraternity to grow this.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: The first question on how integrated we are.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We are not only linking up at the backend but at the front end as well so that at least there is a common database.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: As I have mentioned earlier, they do not need to repeat the same story again.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Different social workers may pick up different issues but, collectively, when we put them all together, some semblance of the truth might emerge and we have better clarity.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: That is something that we are doing and we are unfolding on the ground.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: I would suggest a very big part of it is the relationships.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: The more the different stakeholders get together to know one another, the more they are prepared to share information and a lot of this is tacit information and makes a lot of difference.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We are embarking on the journey and I think we can do better.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Leon Perera, followed by Mr Louis Ng.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: Just one clarification to the Parliamentary Secretary regarding the Maintenance Records Officer that he mentioned which the Minister announced last year.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, this will help the whole process on focusing on which among the spouses can pay and do not want to pay.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: There are cases whereby they really cannot pay.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We believe this will help to somehow close the gap and to improve the processes and the system.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: I share Mr Kok Heng Leun's sentiments about how the wording and how our policies are very important.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: With regard to the two different categories of childcare highlighted by Mr Louis Ng, I personally feel that we should not go into that danger zone of monetising personal relationships.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The Government has been helping so much, to support families to take care of their children.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The calibration needs to be very carefully done.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: If we are not careful, we enter a danger zone where our future generations will start to monetise all aspects of personal relationships.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We want to make sure that it is affordable and we want to support family and child development but we do not want to go that line of monetising personal relationships, and go into the deep end.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: This is an area where we want to identify as many kids as possible in the future.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We are not only going to minimise the incidence of not attending school, but we want to develop the child fully and holistically, so that even the needy among us have the opportunity to develop to the fullest.
